Subject: Access controls and support access — follow-up & next steps

Hi Anna — thanks again for the chat this morning. Quick recap and next steps on the specific items you asked about around access controls and support access: 

1) RBAC & least privilege
- Redwood supports role-based access controls at the org, project, and route levels. You can map roles to your SSO groups (SCIM / SAML). Default roles: Admin, Engineer, Viewer, Support-Limited.
- You wanted confirmation that support cannot view customer request payloads by default — correct. Support-Limited role only has metadata and tracing access; request/response payloads are redacted unless a break-glass event occurs.

2) Break-glass / emergency support access
- Break-glass requires a manager approval flow + audit entry. We also require a justification logged and automatic notification to your security mailbox. Break-glass sessions are time-limited (configurable, default 1 hour) and recorded in audit logs.

3) Support access workflow & least privilege
- We recommend scoped service accounts for integrations and short-lived access tokens for support. Support engineers are given ephemeral sessions that remove token access once the issue is resolved.

4) Audit logs & data retention
- Audit logs include user, action, resource, timestamp, and justification (for break-glass). Logs are available via the Console and exportable to your SIEM. Typical retention options: 90/365/730 days. Let us know which retention you need for FinTrust.

5) Data residency & PII handling
- Hosted Redwood keeps customer data in region-specific clusters. We can configure processing + logs to remain in the US region for your account. PII redaction: by default we persist request metadata and non-sensitive tokens; full request/response bodies are retained per your config and can be automatically redacted or tokenized before storage.

Attachments: I attached a short RBAC overview and a checklist of SOC2 evidence requests we usually see. Please review and tell us which items we should prioritize for your security checklist.

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm desired audit-log retention (90/365/730) and whether you want automatic redaction of PII in stored request bodies.
- We schedule a 30-min follow-up with Stephanie (security PM) and Neha (solutions) to map your SCIM groups and break-glass approval owners.
- We send a redlined SOC2 evidence spreadsheet back to you for any gaps.

Would Friday or early next week work for the follow-up?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Hi Anna / Tom — thanks for these great questions. Answers below, and added proposed configuration options you can pick from before our call on Friday 09:00 PT.

1) Break-glass approvals
- Two-person approval: supported. We can require manager + security engineer to authorize. This is configurable per-organization or per-project. All approvals are written to the audit log with justification and approver identities.

2) Default PII redaction + unredaction flow
- We support automatic PII redaction on ingest (patterns + custom rules). Unredaction is allowed only via a break-glass flow and requires the same multi-person approval. Every unredaction action creates an immutable audit entry with who, when, justification, and a link to the exported content snapshot.

3) Audit log integrity and exports
- We support append-only exports to your S3 with optional object-lock retention (immutable objects) and SHA256 digests for tamper detection. We also publish a signed manifest you can verify.

4) SCIM / Azure AD
- Azure AD group sync is supported. We support groups up to 20k members; nested groups are supported but require a mapping rule (we can help draft that during the call).

5) Operational suggestions (recommended defaults)
- Retention: 365 days for audit logs (we can extend to 730 on request).
- Support role: Support-Limited with metadata-only by default; break-glass enables full payload view for a scoped, time-limited session.
- Monitoring: webhook to FinTrust security mailbox + Slack alert + SIEM export for any unredaction/break-glass event.

Attachments: I attached the RBAC overview again and a draft of the SOC2 evidence checklist with the items you flagged.

Will confirm the calendar invite for Friday 09:00 PT. If you prefer earlier, let me know.

Best,
Marissa
